- Spencer objected to Claude proposing a strategy for the "clincher" project and asked for it to be built directly, with no planning detour.
- Claude built Clincher Sprint 1 as a new repo at `C:\clincher` with one local commit. It is a text-only training loop: log in, pick one of five Got Moles scenarios, talk to an AI customer, end the call, receive a scored scorecard, and retry.
- The database is multi-tenant, employees see only their own sessions, managers see their team, and only the server can write scores. The app recalculates the total score itself rather than trusting the AI's figure.

- Manager pages cover a team overview, playbook and scenario editors, an invite-only "add someone" page, and a note-and-score review. Content draws on the FAQ and the confirmed pricing and claims rules, including the "283+ five-star reviews" wording.
- Limits are 15 sessions per person per day and 40 turns per call, with every AI call logged by token count. The models are `gpt-5.4-mini` for the customer and `gpt-5.5` for scoring.
- Verification: the production build succeeds and all 15 unit tests pass. A test caught a persona leaking real cancellation terms, which Claude rewrote. The app has not yet been run against a live database or the live AI, because no Supabase project or OpenAI key exists.
- Remaining steps need Spencer's accounts: create Supabase and run the migration, fill `.env.local`, seed the first user, then run the app. GitHub, Vercel, Sentry and voice are not yet done.
